title: Your Mum’s Dumpling Recipe
description: Your Mum’s 16 suet dumplings, baked in gravy. Enough for the two of us across two meals.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of round, fluffy dumplings on a rich brown stew in a dark casserole pot.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · dumplings in a venison-stew variation · displayed crop
personalNote: This is your Mum’s recipe. Add the cold water bit by bit and stop when the dough comes together without being sticky. Nice and simple.
equipment: Baking dish with room for 16 dumplings
advancePrep: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Have a baking dish ready with enough room for the dumplings to puff up.
importantNotes: Mum’s full recipe makes 16 dumplings: four dumplings per portion across four portions. That’s dinner and lunch for the two of us, or two dinners with a little extra garlic bread. The gram equivalents are approximate: 5 oz suet is about 142 g and 10 oz flour is about 284 g. If you change the portion control, make proportionally more or fewer dumplings of the same size.

groups.title: Your Mum’s dumplings — full batch makes 16

ingredients.name: Suet
ingredients.note: About 142 g for Mum’s full batch.

ingredients.name: Self-raising flour for dumplings
ingredients.note: About 284 g for Mum’s full batch.

ingredients.name: Cold water for dumplings
ingredients.note: Add a little at a time, only as much as we need for a non-sticky dough.

ingredients.name: Gravy granules
ingredients.note: Use the amount on the packet to make 500 ml of finished gravy for Mum’s full batch.

ingredients.name: Hot water for gravy
ingredients.note: Make the gravy up to this finished volume, following the granule packet.

groups.title: For the second dinner, if we fancy it

ingredients.name: Garlic bread
ingredients.note: Optional to make the second dinner a bit bigger.

steps.title: Put the oven on
steps.description: Preheat the oven to 180°C and get the baking dish ready.

steps.title: Mix Mum’s dry ingredients
steps.description: This is your Mum’s dumpling recipe. Mix the suet, self-raising flour, dried thyme or mixed herbs, and salt together in a bowl first. Her full batch is 5 oz suet, 10 oz flour, 1 teaspoon of herbs and ½ teaspoon of salt.

steps.title: Add cold water bit by bit
steps.description: Add cold water a little at a time and mix between each addition. Stop once we have a dough that comes together without sticking to your hands. We don’t need to guess a fixed amount of water; go by how the dough feels.
steps.doneness: A non-sticky dough that holds together.

steps.title: Shape the dumplings
steps.description: Divide the dough into 16 roughly equal pieces for Mum’s full batch and roll them gently into balls. Try to keep them a similar size so they cook together.
steps.tip: If you change the portion control, make proportionally more or fewer dumplings, keeping each one about the same size.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.description: Make the gravy with the gravy granules and hot water, following the packet. For Mum’s full batch, we want 500 ml of finished gravy. Pour it into the baking dish.

steps.title: Put the dumplings on top and bake
steps.description: Place the dumplings on top of the gravy with a bit of room between them to puff up. Put the dish into the oven at 180°C for the first 10 minutes.

steps.title: Flip halfway and finish baking
steps.description: Carefully flip the dumplings over halfway through, then bake for another 10 minutes. That’s 20 minutes in the oven altogether. Open one to check it’s fluffy and cooked in the middle. If it still has sticky raw dough, give it a little longer.
steps.doneness: Fluffy dumplings cooked in the centre, with hot gravy.

steps.title: Serve the dumplings and gravy
steps.description: Serve straight away with the gravy. Mum’s full batch makes 16 dumplings, enough for dinner and lunch for both of us, or two dinners. Save two portions for the next meal. We can have some garlic bread with the second dinner if we fancy it.

substitutions.title: Thyme or mixed herbs
substitutions.text: Use 1 teaspoon of dried thyme or dried mixed herbs for Mum’s full batch. Whichever one we have is fine.

troubleshooting.title: Getting the dough right
troubleshooting.text: If the dough is still dry and won’t come together, add another little splash of cold water. If it gets sticky, work in a little more self-raising flour until we can shape it. Don’t spiral; we’re just looking for a dough that holds together without sticking.

troubleshooting.title: Are the dumplings done?
troubleshooting.text: Check one after the full 20-minute bake. It should be fluffy and cooked in the middle, with no sticky raw dough. Give it a little longer if it needs it.

storage: For the next meal, cool the dumplings and gravy promptly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze.
reheating: Reheat once until the dumplings and gravy are steaming hot all the way through.
servingSuggestion: Four dumplings per portion. Save two portions for lunch or another dinner, and add garlic bread if we fancy a bit extra with the second dinner.
